title: Change the oil and filter — 5.2L engine
introduction:
This procedure covers the 5.2L engine and contains two filter branches: spin-on and cartridge. Identify the fitted filter before beginning, follow only its branch, and return to the sections marked for all vehicles. The drain plug described here locks with a hand-operated turn; do not apply the threaded-plug method from another engine.

The oil grade and fill quantity come from the [303-01D specifications](#/document/G1800259). Keep that reference available along with the correct filter and seals before draining anything.

items.name: Oil drain equipment
items.detail: Collect oil from both the filter and oil pan.

items.name: Hoist
items.detail: Use the Jacking and Lifting procedure with the vehicle in NEUTRAL.

items.name: Oil filter cap wrench and torque wrench
items.detail: Explicitly required for the spin-on filter; the cartridge housing also has a specified tightening torque.

items.name: Clean lint-free cloth
items.detail: For cartridge-housing threads and sealing surfaces.

items.name: Correct new filter
items.detail: Use the spin-on filter or cartridge element appropriate to the fitted assembly.

items.name: New cartridge-housing O-ring seals, if fitted
items.detail: Do not reuse the old seals. The smallest seal supplied with the filter is not used in this application.

items.name: Clean engine oil
items.detail: Use the grade and fill quantity in 303-01D Engine - 5.2L 32V Ti-VCT specifications.

edits.text: Equipment
Drain the oil
All vehicles — prepare access
Put the transmission in NEUTRAL and position the vehicle on a hoist using [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631) (100-02 Jacking and Lifting, Description and Operation).
Release the retainer and take off the access cover.
If fitted with a spin-on oil filter
Remove the engine oil filter, collect the released oil with Oil Drain Equipment, and discard the filter.
edits.why: The complete spin-on filter is replaced.

edits.text: If fitted with a cartridge oil filter
Loosen the filter housing and let its oil drain into the Oil Drain Equipment.
edits.why: Allowing it to drain first makes the next removal step easier to control.

edits.text: Take the oil filter housing off.
NOTE: Remove every part of the old filter element from both the filter housing and the filter adapter.
Take out the old filter element and discard it.
Remove the old O-ring seals and discard them.
All vehicles — drain and close the oil pan
NOTE: Operate this drain plug by hand for both removal and installation. Do not use tools.
Turn the drain plug counterclockwise 120 degrees by hand, with Oil Drain Equipment ready to catch the oil.
edits.why: This plug releases with a partial turn rather than repeated unscrewing.

edits.text: Pull the released drain plug straight out of the oil pan.
Once the oil has finished draining, push the drain plug back into the oil pan.
NOTICE: Do not overtighten the drain plug. Excessive tightening damages the plug and can also damage the oil pan.
Lock the drain plug by turning it clockwise 120 degrees by hand.
Fit the filter and refill
If fitted with a spin-on oil filter
Coat the new filter’s O-ring seal with clean engine oil.
edits.why: The lubrication is applied to the sealing ring shown in the close-up.

edits.text: Fit the new spin-on oil filter.
Tighten the filter with an oil filter cap wrench and torque wrench to 17 lb.ft (23 Nm).
edits.why: Use the stated torque, rather than judging by how hard the filter feels to turn.

edits.text: If fitted with a cartridge oil filter
Use a clean lint-free cloth to wipe the housing threads and the O-ring sealing surfaces.
Examine the filter housing and its stem for damage, including cracks or separation between the stem and housing. Replace the housing assembly if any damage is present.
edits.why: The reusable housing must be sound before a new element goes inside it.

edits.text: NOTICE: Fit new filter-housing O-ring seals. Reusing the old seals can cause oil leakage.
NOTE: Leave out the smallest O-ring supplied with the filter; this application does not use it.
Install the new filter-housing O-ring seals and coat them with clean engine oil.
edits.why: The illustration identifies the sealing positions.

edits.text: Fit a new oil filter element into the assembly.
Refit the oil filter housing and tighten it to 18 lb.ft (24 Nm).
All vehicles — finish reassembly and fill
Put the access cover back on and secure its retainer.
Fill the engine with clean engine oil, following [Specifications (303-01D Engine - 5.2L 32V Ti-VCT, Specifications)](#/document/G1800259).
edits.why: Use that engine-specific reference for the oil specification and quantity.
